content:
I have maybe a silly question about what the MergeSort complexity file is really showing.

My reading of the file is we reimplement merge sort but taking values in TimeM so that the time complexity can be carried along.

There are some lemmas that show that this TimeM -merge helper agrees on values with the merge from core lean and so these functions compute the same value. However as far as I can tell, this doesn't say anything about the complexity of the merge in core, only that there exists an algorithm that computes the same function in the given time. For example what if the merge_sort in core was actually a bubble sort, these would still agree on values. I guess the value here is that we can then import results from Mathlib to reason about the merge step through referential transparency?

Am I understanding this correctly? I guess this would mean for CSlib we will need to reimplement all "interesting" algorithms from lean / Batteries / Mathlib taking values in TimeM?

Yes that’s correct. Assigning time complexities to lean functions directly is a minefield. Technically it is not even possible as such.

Note that TimeM is just a writer monad. The proof shows that this implementation “refines” the the lean function

I have my reservations about that approach, since we extend the TCB to the metaprogram which constructs an instrumented version of a lean function. This metaprogram is making syntactic transformations which depend on syntactic information such as what operations you count.
